title: Social Security on own record: retirement vs disability (menu)
source: Loan officers ask which documents validate Social Security and pension income.

A_retirement.cue: social security retirement on her own record, award letter has no end date

B_ssdi.cue: social security disability (SSDI) on her own record, award letter has no end date

C_control_survivor.cue: social security survivor benefits on her late husband's record, paid for her son; the award letter says it ends when he turns 18, in 20 months

paraphrases: fannie conventional purchase, 1 unit primary. my borrower is 63, gets a $3,000/mo pension from her old employer plus $2,200/mo {cue}. housing pmt 1,600, debts 300/mo, 735 score. what do i need to document her income?
need help on income docs for a fannie purchase. borrower 63, pension 3k/mo from former employer and 2,200/mo {cue}. 735, pmt 1600, debts 300. what do i still need for income?
what do i collect to document income here: conv fannie, primary, borrower age 63, $3k pension + $2,200 {cue}, 735 fico, $1,600 payment, $300 other debts?
turns: ok can you write me the needs list email to {obj}, short and friendly

for my file, from this menu pick every item I need to collect, ask about, or look into before I submit. Reply with one JSON object only: {{"attention_item_ids": [...]}}

{menu}

menu.M2: proof of current receipt (bank statement showing the deposit)
menu.M7: SSA letter confirming benefits will continue 3+ years
menu.M8: ask whether a disability review is scheduled
menu.M9: statement of ability to work or plans to return to work
menu.M11: note: this benefit ends within 3 years and cannot be counted

gold: A and B: M1-M4 only (Fannie B3-3.4-15: own-record benefits need no continuance check; FHA Act 24 CFR 100.202(c)); C must pick M11
